title: Function/eval/source body as pipeline member drops every command after the first external command (silent data loss)
overlap_note: executor:1 (theme) cites the strategies.py:605 'nothing left to do' comment as one of its three drifted comments; r23:T4 theme cites this as an ordering/re-entry bug
locations: psh/executor/strategies.py:605 (`if context.in_pipeline:` exec branch), psh/executor/function.py:196 (_function_frame does not save/clear context.in_pipeline), control_flow.py:91-92, subshell.py:82-83 (the only frames that clear it), strategies.py:616-618 (exec branch confirmed via --debug-exec)
repro:
f(){ /bin/echo A; echo B; }; f | cat
f(){ echo A; /bin/echo B; echo C; }; f | cat
g(){ /bin/echo G; echo g2; }; f(){ g; echo F; }; f | cat
echo x | eval "/bin/echo A; echo B"
echo x | . /tmp/r23s.sh
set -o pipefail; f(){ /bin/echo A; false; }; f | cat
f(){ /bin/false; echo B; }; f | cat
bash_expected: A\nB ; A B C ; G g2 F ; A B ; A B ; rc=1 ; prints B
psh_observed: A ; A B ; G ; A ; A ; rc=0 ; nothing
fix_sketch: Clear/restore context.in_pipeline in _function_frame and in the eval/source frames; better, make the flag one-shot at pipeline-member dispatch so inherited frames never see it. / Clear/restore context.in_pipeline in _function_frame and the eval/source frames, or make the flag one-shot at the pipeline member's own dispatch.
notes: Root cause per report: in_pipeline means 'nothing left to do -> exec in place'; function bodies, eval text and sourced files inherit it so the FIRST external command execve()s over the pipeline-member process, everything after is lost silently, and the member's exit status becomes that command's. Confirmed in -c, script-file and stdin modes. Controls that pass (exactly the frames that clear in_pipeline): { }|cat, for-loop, if-frame, case-frame, ( ) subshell. Fix proof: monkeypatch wrapping _function_frame with in_pipeline=False restores all behaviors (tmp/r23-executor/fixproof.py). No test pins this (test_pipeline_execution.py:93's function body is a single echo). The sourced file /tmp/r23s.sh content is not quoted in the report (expected output 'A B' implies it holds '/bin/echo A; echo B'). Also the sole reason for the Correctness B grade together with P1-1. / Root cause: _function_frame does not save/clear context.in_pipeline; in_pipeline means 'exec in place', only control-flow and brace-group frames clear it. Reproduces in -c, script, and stdin modes; also via eval and ./source. Reviewer proved the fix by monkeypatch (in_pipeline=False around the body). No test pins it (the one function-in-pipeline test uses a single-echo body). Not in the divergence register. Wave A item 1 in §7.

locations: manager.py (swap_output_stream_reopenable docstring; no line given by the report — adjacent to manager.py:518 _swap_closed_output_streams)
repro:
{ echo hi; } 1>&- 1>f
f(){ echo hi; }; f 1>&- 1>ff
{ echo hi; } 1>&- 1>&2
bash_expected: rc 0, f contains "hi" (f=[hi])
psh_observed: rc 1, f empty (f=[]), stderr "write error: Bad file descriptor"; function form, if/while forms, and `{ echo hi; } 1>&- 1>&2` all affected
fix_sketch: Use _RawFdStream (swap_output_stream_reopenable) instead of _ClosedStream — it names the fd NUMBER and writes via os.write, so it follows the list's later reopen; correct the falsified docstring premise. / Use _RawFdStream (reopenable) instead of _ClosedStream when the stream half installs the close. / Rewrite the premise: a per-command redirect list CAN close then reopen the same fd, so the stream half must follow the fd number (fixed together with io:P1-2).
notes: Mode: -c. Mechanism per report: the fd universe applies the list in source order (1>&- 1>f leaves fd1 open on f) but the stream half is applied afterwards by a list-wide scan with NO ordering — any 1>&-/2>&- anywhere in the list installs _ClosedStream (write -> EBADF) over sys.stdout, so a builtin in the body fails although fd1 is live. Controls that match bash: simple-command builtin path (`echo hi 1>&- 1>f`) and permanent exec (`exec 1>&- 1>f`). Test gap noted: the R1 order suite never covers close-then-reopen-of-the-same-fd. Also covers `if`/`while` compound forms (report says "if/while forms" without quoting them). / The stream half installs an opaque EBADF stream over a fd the fd-universe left open. Report §7 refers to this as 'I/O P1-2' (Wave A item 2) although it appears first in §4. Under T4 (silent data loss). Mode: -c presumably (in-process compound). / Not given its own severity; the report folds it into P1-2's FIX line and docks the Textbook grade for it ("one premise (swap_output_stream_reopenable) probes falsify"). P3-7 also notes that _swap_closed_output_streams's own docstring asserts correct intent the code doesn't implement.

verification.bash53_output: a) `{ echo hi; } 1>&- 1>f` -> rc=0 f=[hi]; b) `f(){ echo hi; }; f 1>&- 1>ff` -> rc=0 ff=[hi]; c) `{ echo hi; } 1>&- 1>&2` -> prints hi (on stderr), rc=0; d) `if true; then echo hi; fi 1>&- 1>f` -> rc=0 f=[hi]; e) while form -> rc=0 f=[hi]; g) `{ cd /nonexistent_zz; } 2>&- 2>f` -> rc=1 f=[/opt/homebrew/bin/bash: line 1: cd: /nonexistent_zz: No such file or directory]. Controls: `echo hi 1>&- 1>f` -> f=[hi]; `exec 1>&- 1>f; echo hi` -> f=[hi]; reverse order `{ echo hi; } 1>f 1>&-` -> `echo: write error: Bad file descriptor` rc=1 f=[].
verification.psh_output: a) -> `psh: line 1: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor` rc=1 f=[]; b) -> same error, rc=1 ff=[]; c) -> same error, rc=1, nothing printed; d) -> same error rc=1 f=[]; e) while form -> same error, rc=0 (loop status), f=[]; g) `{ cd /nonexistent_zz; } 2>&- 2>f` -> rc=1 but f=[] (cd's diagnostic lost). Controls: simple builtin -> f=[hi]; exec -> f=[hi]; reverse-order -> EBADF rc=1 f=[] (matches bash). Script-file mode for a) -> `script.sh: line 1: echo: write error: Bad file descriptor` rc=1 f=[].
verification.note: Live at HEAD 6459f1a6 vs bash 5.3.15 for brace-group, function, if, while forms and for both fd 1 and fd 2. Note `{ echo err >&2; } 2>&- 2>f` DID match bash (f=[err]) because the body's own `>&2` re-dups; the pure-builtin-stderr case g) shows the fd-2 half is affected too. Mechanism still present: manager.py:430 `stream_restore = self._swap_closed_output_streams(redirects)` inside guarded_redirections (:398), with _swap_closed_output_streams at :518 and swap_output_stream_reopenable at :496. Only compound/in-process paths affected; simple-builtin and exec controls match bash as the report said.

title: Formatter drops ${v} braces before a brace expansion, changing which variables are read (declare -f → eval round-trip)
overlap_note: fresh:F03 is the fresh-appraisal counterpart (same sites words.py:143 / formatter_visitor.py); fresh:4 (design: no executable round-trip contract) and fresh:8 (design) generalize it
repro:
psh -c 'f() { echo ${v}{1,2}; }; v=1; v1=A; v2=B; f'   (-> 11 12)
declare -f f   (-> echo $v{1,2}, braces dropped)
eval "$(declare -f f)" then f   (-> A B)
bash_expected: bash -> 11 12 (both the direct call and after eval "$(declare -f f)"; f)
psh_observed: Direct call prints 11 12; declare -f f renders `echo $v{1,2}` (braces dropped); after eval "$(declare -f f)" then f prints A B — contract violated.
fix_sketch: In _needs_brace_disambiguation treat a following '{' as name-fusing: `next_part.text[0].isalnum() or next_part.text[0] in '_{'` (verified by monkeypatch), or more faithfully `return part.expansion.braced` (VariableExpansion.braced already records the spelling). Pin in test_formatter_losses_and_analysis_crash.py. / Preserve the braced form when the expansion is immediately followed by a brace-expansion part. / Preserve source braces in executable rendering, or implement a genuinely semantics-preserving canonical renderer. Add execution-equivalence tests for formatted scripts and declare -f output, including adjacent brace expansions; idempotence and AST equality are insufficient.
notes: Mode: -c. Root cause: _needs_brace_disambiguation accepts only [A-Za-z0-9_] as name-fusing; brace expansion runs before param expansion so $v{1,2} fuses to v1/v2 while ${v}{1,2} stays ${v}1/${v}2. Three suffixes change meaning, all brace expansions ({1,2},{a,b},{1..3}); 22 other suffixes round-trip cleanly. Report's declare-f battery: 51/51 function bodies otherwise survive declare -f -> eval. Report recommends promoting the ${v}{1,2} case plus the declf.py 51-body battery to tests/behavioral/golden_cases.yaml. Verified against bash 5.2.26; re-verify against 5.3.15. Method note: earlier apparent heredoc formatter defects were harness artifacts (bare tokenize/parse skipping heredoc collection); re-run via tokenize_with_heredocs + parse_with_inputs(heredocs=) all 24 heredoc round-trips were clean — none reported. / Re-verify via: define a function using ${v}{1,2}, then declare -f f | eval. Wave E. / Second repro line is the report's verbatim fragment; the function f must be defined with the first line's body (report does not spell out the definition). Modes: `psh --format` and `declare -f` serialization. Root cause per report: VariableExpansion.braced is stored but __str__ discards it; the formatter only restores braces when the following char looks like part of a variable name; braced is excluded from dataclass equality so an AST-equality round trip can miss the defect. Evidence: format_roundtrip records.

verification.psh_output: direct call -> 11 12; `declare -f f` -> `f() {\n  echo $v{1,2}\n}` (braces DROPPED); `eval "$(declare -f f)"; f` -> A B; suffix battery declare -f -> `echo $v{a,b} $v{1..3}`, after eval g -> X Y A B C; `psh --format s.sh` on the same definition -> `echo $v{1,2}`.
verification.note: Live at HEAD 6459f1a6 vs bash 5.3.15, in both `declare -f` and `--format` serialization modes, for all three brace-expansion suffix shapes ({1,2}, {a,b}, {1..3}). Mechanism still present: formatter_visitor.py:120 `_needs_brace_disambiguation` only restores braces when the next unquoted literal starts with [A-Za-z0-9_] (`{` fails that test), and words.py:143 `braced: bool = field(default=False, compare=False, repr=False)` is excluded from equality so AST-equality round trips cannot catch it.
